title: Differential Testing for Sequential to Parallel Transformations
problem: Automated sequential-to-parallel code transformation is error-prone; existing static validation insufficient. Parallel translation errors cause data races, poor performance, rounding issues, unexpected behavior.
motivation: Automated parallelization can yield orders of magnitude speedups but requires validation that parallel program behavior matches sequential version. Current validation methods miss subtle bugs.
method: Seq2ParDiff compares the actual behavior of parallelized code (OpenMP) against the original sequential version by running both on diverse test inputs and checking whether their execution produces identical results in three key areas: program outputs, data stored in memory, and which code branches execute. When the parallel and sequential versions diverge, it identifies a transformation error—such as data races (when multiple threads unsafely access the same data) or incorrect results. By testing real execution rather than analyzing code statically, it catches bugs that static validation alone cannot find.
key_novelty: Seq2ParDiff detects sequential-to-parallel transformation errors by running both versions and comparing their actual execution behavior, catching bugs that static validation misses.
contributions: Seq2ParDiff dynamic validation framework using differential testing
Detection of 20 new faults in OpenMP benchmarks (outperforming static methods)
Identification of faults missed by other tools
Some limitations on data race detection completeness

metrics.new_faults_found: 20 new faults in first benchmark set

limitations: Less effective on certain data race types vs other tools
Abstract-only prevents detail on benchmark sizes, transformation complexity
